title: I vibe coded a real-time multiplayer iPhone game with Claude: what it actually cost me
author: Useful_Ad_52
selftext:
\*\*I'm not a game dev.\*\* 

Over about 2 months I built \*\*Pirate Duel Arena\*\*, a real-time 1v1 pirate cannon duel game for iPhone/iPad, mostly with \*\*Claude (Opus).\*\*

It's live on the App Store now.

\*\*What Claude built with me:\*\* Unity client, online 1v1 matches with a real server (Nakama on a small cloud server), shop + in-app purchases, rankings, cloud builds to TestFlight (I don't own a Mac!). 

\# What it cost (approx):

Claude Max subscription: $100/month × 2 months = $200

\*\*Apple Developer:\*\* $99/year

\*\*Server (DigitalOcean):\*\* $24/month ( \*\*second month only\*\* )

\*\*Domain/website:\*\* $10/y

\*\*Art:\*\* local AI on my own PC ( ComfyUI ).

\*\*Total: \\\~$\\\[333\\\]\*\*

\# What I learned:

\\- Ask for templates and batches early. At first every clothing item took 2–4 hours, one by one. Once i switched to shared templates and batch builds, whole sets finished in a day.

\*\*-\*\* Make the AI try every long job on 1–3 samples first. I once lost 10 hours because it rendered everything before checking a single result.

\\- Test on your real phone early, but not after every step. I don't own a Mac, so every TestFlight build uses GitHub Actions minutes.

\\- Make it write a full plan/roadmap first, then build one small step at a time.

\\- Keep a progress file so each new session knows where you stopped.

Happy to answer anything about the workflow. If you want to try it, it's free: [https://apps.apple.com/app/id6819069267](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6819069267)
